messages:
Anna (Docs): quick heads-up — i'm drafting the 'what's changed' notice for the embed-routing tweak and a short migration blurb. need to sync on wording + SDK snippets. PR coming: #5121
Mike (Product): thanks anna. high level: emphasize no customer data loss, latency small regression for very short sequences, and the recommended quick fix (pin older routing if you need strict determinism).
Jess (SDK): pinged — i'll add python + ts examples. can you confirm the preferred input field name? is it still `routing_preference` or we renamed to `route_hint`?
Anna (Docs): we've standardized on `route_hint` in the runtime PR. pls use `route_hint` in new snippets. also keep the curl example using `-d '{"route_hint":"latency"}'.
Sam (Engineering): @Anna (Docs) FYI there's a known quirk: KV-cache warmup can reorder a few tokens when prefix-caching is enabled. we should add a small known-issue note: "possible minor token reordering during first few requests with prefix cache enabled".
Mike (Product): agreed, that line prevents surprise support tickets. short blurb — 1-2 sentences — with a link to the KB once it's up.
Jess (SDK): will mirror the note in SDK README, and add a guard in examples: `# if you need deterministic output, set route_hint: "conservative"`
Anna (Docs): excellent. here's a compact migration blurb draft — feel free to edit: "If your application relies on exact token ordering, temporarily set `route_hint: \"conservative\"` while we roll out cache alignment. This may increase latency slightly."
Jess (SDK): small nit — change `exact token ordering` -> `deterministic token ordering` (more precise).
Anna (Docs): done. updating PR text. also putting a short 'what changed' bullet: "Embed routing now prioritizes latency by default; use `route_hint` to opt into cost- or determinism-oriented behavior."
Sam (Engineering): for the embed examples, also call out the model variant name change: `embed-fast` -> `embed-fast-v2`. otherwise customers will get 404s.
Anna (Docs): good catch. i'll add a note and an automated redirect mention.
docs-ci: Preview for docs PR #5121 is available: https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/pr-5121 (deploy succeeded) :white_check_mark:
Mike (Product): can someone double-check the short curl snippet renders properly in the mobile view? previous table of examples squashed on mobile.
Jess (SDK): i'll open a tiny CSS tweak PR if needed. for now i'll provide a minimal single-column snippet (no tables).
Anna (Docs): final checklist before merging: 1) SDK snippets updated (jess) 2) KB link placeholder for token reordering (sam) 3) model name + redirect note (sam) 4) preview review / mobile check (mike) 5) add TOC anchor for "known issues" (anna)
Mike (Product): timeline — want this live before EOD Friday. is that feasible?
Sam (Engineering): we can land runtime redirect + KB draft by Thursday.
Jess (SDK): SDK snippets and README updates by Thursday evening.
Anna (Docs): i'll aim to merge the doc PR after all checks on Friday morning. tagging reviewers: @Mike (Product) for final copy, @Sam (Engineering) for the KB and model-name confirmation.
Mike (Product): sounds good. feel free to squash commits when merging. :+1:
Anna (Docs): thanks team — i'll post a short announcement blurb in #announcements once live.
Anna (Docs): (edit) one more tiny addition: include example with streaming flag, people often miss that. code: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-fast-v2","route_hint":"latency","stream":true,"input":"hello"}'
```
Jess (SDK): looks good. i'll ensure the SDK streaming sample matches the curl body.
docs-ci: Preview updated for PR #5121: https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/pr-5121 (build 7) :white_check_mark:
